 News Flash
 Intern Jackie Garcia: My Experience as a Student Poll Worker
 Elections
 Posted on November 20, 2026 
 By Jackie Garcia, Elections intern 
When I first heard about the opportunity of helping people within the community to vote, I was very proud of the fact that I was willing to do something new that also benefited my community. While doing my internship with Nevada County Elections, Public Information Contractor Lisa Renner and Registrar of Voters Armando Salud-Ambriz reached out to me about this opportunity, and I am very grateful till this day. Ever since 8th grade I always asked myself the same question “What happens during an Election Day?” Growing up I've always brought that same question to me everywhere. Now, I am very proud I was able to make this question into reality and gain knowledge from it but also help explain it to the people in my community who face language barriers.
 The most meaningful part of my day was knowing that I really made an impact being there. When I arrived, my task was to help print out ballots and hand them out to people. While doing this I heard somebody that was working with me say, “Does anybody here speak Spanish?” I raised my hand instantly and helped at least 10 people. I helped explain their next steps and broke them down in simpler words so they wouldn't feel confused. The day was long, but the time felt like it was going very fast. While printing ballots and scanning QR codes, it was very interesting how many people participated in voting. In certain times we would get lines that would go outside and sometimes we would get just a few people. 
 What I'm going to take away from this opportunity is how much impact the youth have today. When I first got the news that 15 students were going to help out on Election Day, I realized how much the youths’ involvement can really help the community in many different ways. The youths' involvement shows how though we might not know everything about elections, we are using our voice to help people in our community get more involved. While printing out ballots I heard a large number of people coming in and saying that they loved having students involved with helping out on Election Day. Hearing this from many people in my community really made me proud of the work I did. I am very grateful for Lisa and Armando who reached out to me about this opportunity. Working on Election Day may seem like something you might worry about, but I learned that you are not alone and we work together as a team.
